clue.text: Score with a flat note written here, perhaps, in LA?

definitions.text: note written here, perhaps, in LA

parts.note: to score a surface is to scratch it
pad is slang for a flat or apartment, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: A musician jots down a melody with a flat note, perhaps somewhere in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'flat note' look musical; 'Score' is to scratch and 'a flat' is a pad. 'in LA' hints at the American flavour of the term.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough notebook for jotting things down quickly, the place where a memo might be scribbled.

clue.text: Comparatively uneven EP? Sort it out!

indicators.note: sort it out tells us to rearrange the letters of EP and SORT IT

explanation.surface: A record reviewer complains that an extended-play disc is patchy and demands it be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: EP (extended play record) plus SORT IT rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchier or more blotchy in quality, so more irregular than something else.

clue.text: Flyer showing a current mother holding 23A? On the contrary

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: mother holding something would put it inside MA
reverses the containment just stated, so the naval letters hold the mother instead

parts.note: 23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Navy, RN
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A pilot shows off a mother cradling a member of the armed forces, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'mother holding 23A', so RN holds MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flies an aircraft, especially a member of an air force.

clue.text: Dropping improvisation in jazz

definitions.meaning: animal droppings, as tracked by naturalists
wordless vocal improvising, as made famous by Ella Fitzgerald

explanation.surface: A jazz singer gives up improvising.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both animal dung and nonsense-syllable jazz singing, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: This is set to flap around, eating a little apple

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take something inside them as if swallowing it
the letters of set to flap are moved around into a new order
a little of apple is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Something is about to flutter while munching a bit of apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' is the definition, the whole clue describing it: SET TO FLAP rearranged ('around') with A, the first of 'apple', inside ('eating'). The soft palate does flap, in snoring, and food passes it when eating.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy back part of the roof of the mouth, which vibrates in snoring and helps in swallowing.

clue.text: Radio broadcaster has last word in North American capital

indicators.note: the broadcaster and last word go inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, presents radio shows
amen is said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A radio presenter gets the final say in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North American capital' looks like one phrase, but the city is in Africa: it is the capital of Chad.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city and seat of government of Chad in central Africa.

clue.text: Model getting out of car under 23A tree

indicators.note: in a down answer, what comes under follows

parts.note: 23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Air Force, RAF

indicators.note: the model letter leaves the car name

parts.note: Fiat is an Italian car maker
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so Model gives T

explanation.surface: A fashion model climbs out of a car beneath a service-themed tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is not a fashion model but the T of Ford's Model T, removed from FIAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm from Madagascar whose leaf fibre is used for weaving and tying.

clue.text: Skunk with damaged coat

indicators.note: a damaged coat has its letters knocked into another order

explanation.surface: A skunk with a ruined fur.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American skunk-like animal, the coati, often confused; here a crossword-only name for a skunk.

clue.text: Lively work in Channel Islands, feeding goat after dropping 23A

indicators.note: the islands' letters go into the shortened goat sign like food
the goat sign has the naval letters taken away

parts.note: Capricorn is the zodiac sign of the goat
23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Navy, RN

explanation.surface: A spirited piece in Jersey or Guernsey is fed to a goat once something is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goat' is the zodiac sign Capricorn; 'after dropping' removes the naval letters, leaving CAPRICO for 'feeding' to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a free, lively musical composition, often fanciful in form.

clue.text: Backing Irish politician over 23A plan

indicators.note: the reversed letters go over, that is around, the service letters
the politician's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a TD, Teachta Dala, is a member of the Irish parliament
23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Air Force, RAF

explanation.surface: An Irish politician supports a scheme for the air force.
explanation.walkthrough: A TD is a member of the Dail, Ireland's lower house. 'Backing' turns it to DT, and 'over' here means wrapped over.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary version or outline of something, such as a first sketch of a scheme.

clue.text: Try cooking meat to provide tasty starters

indicators.note: cooking the meat and the starters mixes up their letters
starters means the opening letters of to, provide and tasty

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to cook meat so as to serve appetising first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like a course of the meal; it takes T, P, T from 'to provide tasty', mixed with MEAT ('cooking').
explanation.definitionFit: An effort or go at something, a synonym of the noun try.

clue.text: Group taking time to 23A football club around lunchtime

parts.note: 23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Air Force, RAF

indicators.note: the club letters sit around the lunchtime letter

parts.note: one o'clock is lunchtime, and one is I

explanation.surface: A party takes time off to visit a football club around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' is the 1960s British rock band Traffic. 'lunchtime' is one o'clock, giving I, which goes inside FC.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic was a British rock band formed by Steve Winwood, so an example of a musical group.

clue.text: The Stones, all in a heap about "first-class" 23A

definitions.text: The Stones, all in a heap

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
A1 means first-class, written AI
23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Navy, RN

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones are lumped together around a top-notch service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Stones' suggests the rock band; it is just stones piled up. A1 (first-class) is written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of stones piled up as a landmark or memorial on a hill or path.

clue.text: Help RAF at new illuminated airstrip

indicators.note: the letters of help RAF at are made into something new

explanation.surface: Assist the air force with a fresh landing strip lit up for night flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway lined with flares or lights so aircraft can land in the dark.

clue.text: Literary lord dressing neatly (plus fours, mostly)

indicators.note: dressing works the letters into a fresh arrangement, as one dresses a salad
mostly means fours minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A lord in a book wears neat clothes, including golfing plus fours, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plus fours' are baggy golfing trousers, but 'plus' just links NEATLY and FOUR (FOURS 'mostly'), mixed by 'dressing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Lord Fauntleroy is the title character of Frances Hodgson Burnett's children's novel.

clue.text: Bloomer involving footballers and drugs, say

parts.note: Hearts, Heart of Midlothian, is an Edinburgh football club

indicators.note: the two drug letters wrap around the for-example letters

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so two of them make drugs
as means for example, like say

explanation.surface: A blunder involving soccer players and narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flower. HEARTS is a Scottish football club, Heart of Midlothian.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild pansy, a flowering plant, so something that blooms.

clue.text: "Drama doesn't have to go to bed with high art", as a rude RADA motto

definitions.text: "Drama doesn't have to go to bed with high art", as a rude RADA motto

parts.words: "Drama doesn't have to go to bed with high art", as a rude RADA motto
parts.note: the Latin motto of the Royal Air Force, through adversity to the stars, rudely recast as advice for drama students: sleep your way to stardom

explanation.surface: A cheeky slogan for the drama school RADA says actors need not sleep with serious art.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London. The Latin 'per ardua' can be read rudely as by way of something hard, and 'ad astra' as to stardom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto of the Royal Air Force, meaning through adversity to the stars.

clue.text: State once more taking income finally secured by 23A company

indicators.note: the closing letter is held inside the service letters

parts.note: 23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Air Force, RAF

indicators.note: finally means the closing letter of income

parts.note: a firm is a company

explanation.surface: A business guaranteed by the air force declares its income again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun but is the verb; 'secured by' means held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert or declare something again, confirming it as true.

clue.text: From which baby eats, half served up in both late afternoon and early evening?

definitions.text: both late afternoon and early evening?

parts.note: a baby feeds from a teat

indicators.note: in a down answer, served up means the letters are written upwards

parts.note: semi means half, as in semicircle

explanation.surface: A feeding baby eats, with half the meal brought out in both late afternoon and early evening.
explanation.walkthrough: SEMI (half) reversed ('served up') gives IMES. The question mark admits that late afternoon and early evening are both times for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasions when an afternoon or evening meal of tea is taken, which fall around five or six o'clock.

clue.text: Strip, having at last removed one's cloak

indicators.note: at last picks the closing letter of removed

parts.note: one is I, so one's is IS
a mantle is a loose cloak

explanation.surface: Someone undresses, having finally taken off a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like undressing, which the surface encourages; it means take apart. 'one's' gives I'S, I being one.
explanation.definitionFit: To take apart a machine or structure piece by piece.

clue.text: Second 23A in film about attack with flying arms

indicators.note: the service letters go inside the reversed film title
the film title is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an alien
23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Air Force, RAF

explanation.surface: A second air force unit appears in a movie about an aerial assault.
explanation.walkthrough: ET reversed ('about') gives TE, with RAF placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Skill landing 23A in court

indicators.note: the service letters land inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: 23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Air Force, RAF

explanation.surface: Expertise is shown in bringing an air force plane down on a court.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft means skill in making things, as in arts and crafts.

clue.text: A 23A in church, in which one has wine?

indicators.note: a plus the service letters go inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Air Force, RAF

explanation.surface: An airman in church, where someone takes communion wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which one has wine' points to communion in church; it describes the jug that holds wine at table.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass jug for serving wine or water at the table.

clue.text: African native ruminating online on girlfriend hosting one 23A

indicators.note: in an across answer, online on girlfriend puts E after her
the girlfriend letters host, that is contain, the other pieces

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Air Force, RAF
e- as in email means online, giving E

explanation.surface: An African chats online with a girlfriend who is hosting an airman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African native ruminating' is the whole definition: 'ruminating' means chewing the cud, not thinking. 'on' places E after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is native to Africa and, like a cow, chews the cud.

clue.text: Letter about 23A's source of personnel for battleship

indicators.note: the letter's spelled-out name goes about the other pieces

parts.note: gee is the spelling of the letter G
23A names a branch of the armed forces; here the Royal Air Force, RAF, with its S

indicators.note: source of means the opening letter of personnel

explanation.surface: A letter concerning the air force's supply of crew for a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: The German pocket battleship scuttled off Montevideo in 1939.
explanation.definitionFit: The Admiral Graf Spee was a German heavy cruiser called a pocket battleship.

clue.text: Receives this, perhaps, playing after loss of point?

definitions.text: Receives this, perhaps, playing after loss of point?

indicators.note: playing shuffles the remaining letters into a new order
the word receives loses one point letter

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: In tennis, a player receives this, perhaps, play resuming once a point is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: RECEIVES minus an E (a compass 'point') is rearranged ('playing'). The whole clue also describes it: after losing a point the receiver faces the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a player receives the serve, the stroke that starts each point.

clue.text: See 22
With reference to a sergeant flying primarily with other ranks in 23A

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of a, sergeant and flying

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks

explanation.surface: Concerning a sergeant airborne mainly with non-commissioned personnel in the air force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 23A' only sets the military scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning regarding or concerning, introducing the topic in question.

clue.text: Fever? Dose is wrong — gives too much for stomach to digest

definitions.text: gives too much for stomach to digest

indicators.note: a dose that is wrong is mixed up, so the letters of fever and dose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient with a temperature is given the wrong amount of medicine, too much to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide more food than is needed or healthy, beyond what the stomach can manage.
